lines.say: Anthropic replaced Git, the tool that tracks every code change. Why?
lines.text: Anthropic replaced Git, the tool that tracks every code change. Why?

lines.say: It built its own tool, Scion. All its code sits in one store. We call it a monorepo.
lines.text: It built its own tool, Scion. All its code sits in one store. We call it a monorepo.

lines.say: AI programs write code all day. We call them agents.
lines.text: AI programs write code all day. We call them agents.

lines.say: A machine checks each of their changes. We call this a C I job.
lines.text: A machine checks each of their changes. We call this a CI job.

lines.say: Take one fix to payments slash refund dot P Y. Its C I job needs the code.
lines.text: Take one fix to payments/refund.py. Its CI job needs the code.

lines.say: It asks a central computer. We call it the server.
lines.text: It asks a central computer. We call it the server.

lines.say: The server sends a copy. We call this step a checkout.
lines.text: The server sends a copy. We call this step a checkout.

lines.say: Git sends every file, and every past version: how it looked before each change. So people can work offline, with no connection.
lines.text: Git sends every file, and every past version: how it looked before each change. So people can work offline, with no connection.

data.pastSub: HOW IT LOOKED BEFORE EACH CHANGE

lines.say: That suits most projects. But here, the files alone fill over twenty five gigabytes. One film is a few gigabytes.
lines.text: That suits most projects. But here, the files alone fill over 25 gigabytes. One film is a few gigabytes.

lines.say: For these changes, Anthropic runs about twenty five million C I checkouts a day.
lines.text: For these changes, Anthropic runs about 25 million CI checkouts a day.

lines.say: If each took those twenty five gigabytes, the servers would send twenty five million times twenty five gigabytes a day. That is over six hundred million gigabytes, or over a hundred million films.
lines.text: If each took those 25 gigabytes, the servers would send 25 million times 25 gigabytes a day. That is over 600 million gigabytes, or over a hundred million films.

data.tag: IF EVERY CHECKOUT TOOK THOSE 25 GB

lines.say: But C I jobs never work offline. They run on Anthropic's own computers, always connected to the server.
lines.text: But CI jobs never work offline. They run on Anthropic's own computers, always connected to the server.

lines.say: So they need no full copy.
lines.text: So they need no full copy.

lines.say: Git sends every past version. Scion keeps them on the server instead. The machine gets only the files it needs.
lines.text: Git sends every past version. Scion keeps them on the server instead. The machine gets only the files it needs.

lines.say: To find refund dot P Y, the machine gets a list of what is in the main folder. We call such a list a tree.
lines.text: To find refund.py, the machine gets a list of what is in the main folder. We call such a list a tree.

lines.say: That tree points to the payments folder's tree, which points to refund dot P Y.
lines.text: That tree points to the payments folder's tree, which points to refund.py.

lines.say: Each file version gets an I D made from its contents. We call it a content address.
lines.text: Each file version gets an ID made from its contents. We call it a content address.

lines.say: When the fix edits the file, it gets a new address. An old address always holds the same contents.
lines.text: When the fix edits the file, it gets a new address. An old address always holds the same contents.

lines.say: So any machine can keep copies and reuse them. We call such a store of copies a cache.
lines.text: So any machine can keep copies and reuse them. We call such a store of copies a cache.

lines.say: Each machine has its own cache. Machines in the same region also share one, so few ask the server.
lines.text: Each machine has its own cache. Machines in the same region also share one, so few ask the server.

lines.say: Machine cache, shared cache, server: we call these three layers tiers.
lines.text: Machine cache, shared cache, server: we call these three layers tiers.

lines.say: When a cache holds the file, we call it a cache hit. Machine cache and shared cache each hit over ninety nine percent of the time.
lines.text: When a cache holds the file, we call it a cache hit. Machine cache and shared cache each hit over 99% of the time.

lines.say: Few requests reach the server, and none for a whole copy. Less to send means less computer power and memory, a computer's short-term storage.
lines.text: Few requests reach the server, and none for a whole copy. Less to send means less computer power and memory, a computer's short-term storage.

lines.say: Anthropic reports two hundred times less of both than the old Git servers.
lines.text: Anthropic reports 200 times less of both than the old Git servers.

lines.say: Anthropic says Scion fits only the largest monorepos. Normal projects have small copies, so Git stays right.
lines.text: Anthropic says Scion fits only the largest monorepos. Normal projects have small copies, so Git stays right.
